idea-plugin.name: Incredibuild Build Acceleration
idea-plugin.description:
Incredibuild Build Acceleration builds your project through Incredibuild directly from the IDE — a Rust/Cargo project from RustRover (or IntelliJ IDEA with the Rust plugin), or a CMake project from CLion.

Incredibuild is a build acceleration tool that distributes compilation work across the free cores of multiple machines on your network (or in the cloud), cutting build times without requiring any changes to your code or project structure.

A dedicated Incredibuild menu accelerates a build on demand. In RustRover:

  • Build — builds whatever the IDE's own Build Project would build, through Incredibuild.
  • Rebuild — cleans the Cargo workspace first, then builds it.

In CLion:

  • Build — builds the target behind the selected run configuration, through Incredibuild.
  • Rebuild — cleans and builds that same target in one accelerated step.
  • Build All — builds every target in the active CMake profile.

Stop Build — cancels the build in progress — is available either way.

In RustRover, the IDE's own build actions can be accelerated as well. Turn on Accelerate the IDE's own build actions in Settings | Tools | Incredibuild, and two things change: Build Project goes through Incredibuild, and so does the build that runs before Run and Test. The commands and keyboard shortcuts stay exactly where they are — only what happens underneath changes. The setting is off by default. While it is off — or if Incredibuild is not installed on the machine — those actions behave exactly as they do without this plugin. The actions in the Incredibuild menu always use Incredibuild, whichever way the setting is set.

Either way the accelerated build runs the same command the IDE itself would have run: the selected run configuration, build profile and target selection are respected for Cargo, and in CLion the accelerated build runs cmake's own generator-agnostic cmake --build against whichever build directory, toolchain and compiler the active CMake profile is already configured with, so it works the same way whether that profile uses Ninja, Unix Makefiles or NMake Makefiles. The same settings page configures how many parallel jobs accelerated builds request.

Works with Incredibuild on both Windows and Linux.
